mutations.before: const briefFetchKey = brief === undefined || cell === undefined ? undefined : previewFetchKey(brief, cell.productId);
mutations.because: CC2's fix is keying the fetch on the brief's CONTENT (previewFetchKey), not its object identity. Restoring identity as the key reintroduces the defect: toBrief(state) builds a new brief object on every keystroke, so a look-preserving edit (typing in targetAudience) fires a fresh /preview-frame request again. Caught by a CALL COUNT, not a mount count.

isRailWideEnough is the JS-side mirror of the row's own CSS container query (CC2): below 56rem the rail is CSS-hidden but stays mounted, and withholding `brief` is the only thing that stops usePreviewFrame from building a request there. Feeding the dock `previewBrief` unconditionally lets a rail nobody can see keep fetching. Caught by a CALL COUNT ("nothing fetches below the breakpoint"), not a mount count — the rail's own mount is unaffected by this mutation.

previewBrief is deliberately memoised on a narrower key than draftBrief (CC1/CC2's memo boundary) so the preview dock and its fetch can bail out on a look-preserving keystroke. The YAML view is the rail's read-only SECOND view (D61) and must stay live: feeding it the memoised previewBrief instead of the live draftBrief makes it go stale on exactly the fields the memo key ignores (e.g. targetAudience). Caught by a staleness ASSERTION on rendered content, not a call count or a mount count.
